name: Jodie Barr

summary.text: Jodie Barr, age 66, is the Libertarian Party nominee for Colorado state treasurer in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She says she spent years running a small business, including managing payroll, and has studied state and municipal finance; she has not held elected office.

experience.text: Ran a small business and managed its payroll, which she says shaped her view that 'the Treasurer's job is to act as a fiduciary for taxpayers, not an extension of the legislature's spending appetite.'

positions.source_title: State Treasurer | Grantham, Bridges, Barr seek top financial position
positions.quote: Defend TABOR against workarounds that spend past voter-approved limits.
positions.note: Listed among her stated priorities as treasurer; not a direct mention of Proposition NN by name.

research_notes: No campaign website found (The Ballot Brief confirms none was found as of Sept. 8, 2026). Barr has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey. Her only substantive media coverage found is the Oct. 2, 2026 Colorado Politics joint candidate questionnaire, which covered unclaimed-property and PERA questions that don't map to any of the 25 tracked statements; only her TABOR-related answer was codeable. No positions found on any social-axis statement (abortion, guns, immigration, etc.) — plausible given she has never held office and has a limited campaign footprint, but not exhaustively confirmed beyond the sources above given the short-profile effort budget. Second pass 2026-10-14: the Denver Post's Oct. 3, 2026 treasurer candidate Q&A states 'Marilee Langner Sturgis and Jodie Barr did not return the questionnaire,' confirming the gap already noted; the Colorado Sun's Amendment 87 and Proposition 136 explainers also do not name her. No new positions were added.
